name: Cebalrai
description: A giant of type K2 III 25.1 parsecs away, 12.2 times the Sun's width: its disc was measured with the Navy Precision Optical Interferometer.

radius.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 161096: radius 12.17 +/- 0.06 solar radii (Table 5), from the limb-darkened angular diameter 4.511 +/- 0.011 mas (NPOI, Table 4) and the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax

mass.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 161096: mass 1.44 +/- 0.16 solar masses (Table 6), from the PARAM Bayesian fit to PARSEC isochrones at the measured temperature; the paper calls its masses estimates only

temperature.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 161096: effective temperature 4559 +/- 57 K (Table 5), from the angular diameter and the bolometric flux of the SED fit

distance.source: Baines et al. (2018), AJ 155, 30, HD 161096: the Hipparcos (van Leeuwen 2007) parallax the radius was computed with (Table 1), 39.85 +/- 0.17 mas, inverted

text.card: A giant of type K2 III, 25 parsecs away: 12.2 times the Sun's width and 58 times its light.
text.introduction: Its disc spans 4.511 milliarcseconds, which gives 12.17 solar radii and 4,559 K at its surface.
text.locator: Tables 1, 4 and 5, HD 161096: parallax, limb-darkened diameter, radius, Teff

radialVelocity.source: SIMBAD's radial velocity for Gaia DR3 4473334474604992384 (quality A), from 2018A&A...616A...7S; Gaia DR3 measures none
